about: Socially Awkward Penguin is a cutout of an Adélie penguin waddling to the right, one flipper lifted and its head turned away, set on a background of alternating blue triangles that radiate from the center. Its stiff, mid-stumble posture looks like someone trying very hard to exit a conversation. Captions narrate small, painfully relatable social blunders in two beats: a normal situation, then the clumsy way you handled it. Waving back at someone who was waving at the person behind you, answering "you too" to a waiter who said "enjoy your meal" is the kind of moment this penguin was made for.
origin: The penguin comes from a National Geographic wildlife photo by George F. Mobley. Pasted onto the blue advice-animal background, it became one of the best-known image macros of the late 2000s and early 2010s, alongside a confident "Socially Awesome Penguin" variant.
usage:
The top box describes an ordinary social situation in a few words, written like an action: "start telling joke", "waiter says enjoy your meal". The bottom box is the awkward way it goes wrong: "forget punchline", "you too".

Short, clipped phrasing in the old advice-animal style works best. The more universal the cringe, the harder it lands, so pick moments most people have lived through: phones, small talk, greetings, video calls and group chats.
